To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Internet retailers are more price competitive than traditional retailers, (ii) Internet retailers are less price competitive than traditional retail stores in the presence of manufacturers that limit the sale of their product by Internet retailers, and (iii) the Internet retailers that are most price competitive are the ones that are least likely to sell products from manufacturers that limit the distribution of their products by the Internet.

manufacturers of fragrances, DVD Players and side-by-side fridges limit the distribution of their products to brick and mortar stores and prevent Internet retailers from selling their products at low prices.

manufacturers that limit the sale of their branded products by Internet retailers also tend to limit the sale of those products by Internet retailers who offer deep discounts, and manufacturer websites tend to sell their products at higher prices than Internet retailers who are authorized to sell the product.
